links.title: Children, but not language models, show accelerating returns in word learning

evidence: Abstract: 'language models ... do not accelerate. Instead, they show constant proportional returns on new data, consistent with scaling laws.'

Section 'Fitting the accumulator model': 'substantial improvements in item-level expected log predictive density ... (LOO ELPD >760 for all five datasets)' with kappa estimates 10.6-13.3 across five longitudinal datasets, N_total=1841.

Supplementary 'Language model training': GPT-2-small (124M) on 24M-word CHILDES; 180 models for the development sequence and 8x12x3x2=576 models for composition analysis; scaling fit E~2.94, B~312, beta~0.32, R^2=0.998.

Supplementary 'Matched Estimation of Acceleration': applying the LM four-parameter logistic estimator to child data yields corrected kappa 10.42-13.81 vs LM 1.16 [0.93, 1.46], addressing estimator-mismatch objections.
Discussion: 'our evidence is based on statistical fit and model comparison, rather than a causal manipulation. More work is required to test the accumulator as a mechanistic account.'
Availability note: code at github.com/mcfrank/acceleration, fits archived on Redivis, trained LMs on HuggingFace (childes-gpt2-ladder), data via wordbankr/childesr.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A cognitive-science paper that uses language models as a comparison system rather than advancing LLM methodology; it is relevant to LLM interests (scaling laws, the child-LM data gap, BabyLM-style sample-efficient training) but its core contribution is a psychometric model of children's vocabulary growth. The 'accelerating accumulator' Rasch model with per-child acceleration kappa is a novel synthesis linking IRT growth curves to neural scaling laws, building on Hidaka (2013), McMurray (2007), and Chang & Bergen (2022). Rigor is high: Bayesian Stan fits with convergence criteria (R-hat<1.01), nested model ablations M0-M3, LOO ELPD comparisons with SEs, prospective cross-validation on 371 Norwegian children, and extensive robustness checks (2PL IRT, item-selection narrowing, data-quality filter sensitivity, log vs linear age, hierarchical pooling, matched LM-style estimator applied to children). Evidence is quantitative and strong (kappa 10.6-13.3 across five datasets; LM beta~0.32, R^2=0.998), though the children-vs-LM claim rests on small GPT-2 models trained on 24M CHILDES words plus assumed input-rate calibrations, and the author concedes the evidence is 'statistical fit and model comparison, rather than a causal manipulation'. CDI parent-report production data and constant-rate input assumptions add noise. Cross-linguistic coverage (English, Norwegian, Japanese) plus re-analysis of four architectures supports generalizability, though extension to large-scale LMs is inferential. Reproducibility is excellent: public code, archived fits, and all trained LMs released.

primary_link.title: Children, but not language models, show accelerating returns in word learning

radar.summary: Children learn hundreds of words over the first years of their lives, in a process that begins slowly but quickly picks up speed. Prior models describe vocabulary growth as evidence accumulation over time. Here we show that the process is best characterized as accelerating accumulation: children learn more from each additional unit of linguistic experience than they did from the one before. In contrast to children, language models -- even those trained on child-directed speech -- do not accelera
radar.summary_zh: 兒童在前幾年學會數百個詞，過程由慢轉快。先前模型將詞彙成長描述為證據隨時間累積，本文則顯示此過程最佳刻畫為「加速累積」：兒童從每一單位語言經驗學到的比前一單位更多。作者發展加速累積器心理計量模型，以 Rasch 模型結合隨發展對數時間增長的能力項（加速指數 κ），擬合五個縱貫 CDI 資料集（美式英語、挪威語、日語，共 1841 名幼兒）。結果 κ 估計達 10.6–13.3，穩健拒絕純累積器（κ=1），且學習較晚詞彙所需曝光次數隨年齡呈指數下降。相對地，即使以兒童導向語料（CHILDES，約 2400 萬詞）訓練的 GPT-2，其逐詞 κ 值聚於 1 附近，展現與 scaling laws 一致的固定比例報酬；語言模型的成比例報酬為常數，兒童則隨發展上升。此結果為兒童與語言模型間的數量級資料差距提供候選解釋：兒童對學習輸入的使用效率隨發展提升，包括詞彙辨識加速與「學習如何學習」。限制包括依賴家長報告的 CDI、屬統計擬合而非因果操弄，且未釐清促成加速的具體機制。此發現為比較人類與人工學習者、以及研究樣本效率奠定了基礎。
radar.title: Children, but not language models, show accelerating returns in word learning
radar.title_zh: 兒童而非語言模型，在詞彙學習中展現加速報酬

links.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments

evidence: Abstract/Contributions (Section 1): 'We show that three activation-reading interpretability tools, all of which provide uplift in prior auditing games on fine-tuned models, provide no uplift on our evaluation.'
Appendix C.3, Table 5: transcript-only baselines 0.819 (GPT-5.5), 0.793 (Gemini-3.1-Pro), 0.814 (Opus 4.8); 'No tool beats its own baseline for any agent; Gemini is actively hurt by the NLA and SAE.'
Section 4.4/Figure 6: 'Both trained models improve substantially over the base model (Figure 6) and land within ±0.03 AUROC of the Opus reference on every set.'

Section 2.2: claim labeling thresholds 'true if its edit moved the behavior rate by at least 50 percentage points and false if it moved the rate by at most 15', 30pp prediction threshold in claim template (Appendix B.4).
Appendix F: unfiltered deltas over Opus reference '+0.015 [+0.002, +0.027]' (Qwen3-8B) and '+0.033 [+0.021, +0.044]' (Qwen3.5-397B), showing filters do not create the result.
Appendix D.4: 'In neither direction does the self predictor beat the cross predictor (Figure 8)' — no evidence of privileged access with size-matched 23,944-example training sets.
Section 5/Appendix A.1: explicit limitation that the evaluation is a proxy since 'anyone with sampling access to the target model could answer our evaluation by running the counterfactual directly.'
Appendix B.5, Table 3: per-investigation cost $1.9 (evaluation) and $0.9 (training), total run costs $3.3k and $26k, supporting cost/scale claims.
Release claim (Section 1): 'We release all code, models, and datasets, including investigation runs on five target models... https://github.com/adamkarvonen/chive' — supports reproducibility.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM methodology paper squarely on-topic: agentic pipelines, interpretability tool evaluation (SAEs, activation oracles, NLAs), counterfactual simulatability, CoT faithfulness, and AI-safety auditing. Novel contribution is CHIVE, which moves counterfactual explanation evaluation from planted-hint settings to naturally-occurring behaviors at scale. Rigor is high: two-three target models, three predictor families, hyperparameter sweeps (Table 4), bootstrap CIs, filter ablations on the unfiltered dataset (Appendix F), a self-vs-cross privileged-access control (D.4), and a KL-regularization control (D.5). Evidence is quantitative and mostly in-text (e.g., baseline AUROC 0.814 vs tool 0.808-0.812 in C.3; unfiltered deltas +0.015/+0.033 with CIs). Limitations are honestly discussed, including the proxy argument that anyone with sampling access can run the counterfactual directly, and the read-only ceiling. Main weaknesses: some headline results live in figures without full numeric tables, LLM-judge dependence for screening/filters (mitigated by labels coming from resampling, not judge judgment), and the interpretability null result may partially reflect tool design rather than inherent limits. Reproducibility is strong with released code, models, datasets, costs, and verbatim formats.

primary_link.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments

top5.summary: Many areas of AI research, such as language model interpretability and chain of thought faithfulness, seek to explain model behaviors. But what constitutes a "good" explanation? In this work, we evaluate explanations through the lens of counterfactual simulatability-whether the explanation is useful for predicting model behaviors on related counterfactual inputs. To this end, we introduce CHIVE (Counterfactual Hypothesis Investigation Via Edits), a novel agentic pipeline that identifies unexpect
top5.summary_zh: 這篇論文探討一個根本問題:什麼才算對語言模型行為的「好解釋」?作者採用反事實可模擬性(counterfactual simulatability)的觀點:好的解釋應能幫助預測模型在相關反事實輸入上的行為。他們提出 CHIVE,一個代理式流程,自動在真實對話(WildChat)中取樣數萬個提示詞、篩選非預期行為,以反事實提示詞編輯調查並驗證成因,產生數千筆附反事實證據的行為解釋。這些資料有兩種應用。第一,評估三種讀取激活值的可解釋性工具(activation oracles、自然語言自動編碼器、稀疏自動編碼器)能否提升預測代理判斷反事實結果的能力;在兩個目標模型與三個預測模型家族上,皆無工具優於僅讀對話紀錄的基線,主因是工具輸出鮮少明確陳述因果關係。第二,以 CHIVE 資料訓練模型預測自身行為,能泛化到 held-out 的植入線索情境(MMLU 線索、AITA 諂媚測試)與分布外的 PETRI 來源,表現接近 Opus 參考基準;但訓練開放式自我解釋成效好壞參半,常出錯的自信陳述反而誤導強大的模擬器。此外未見自我訓練優於交叉訓練的特權存取證據。主要限制在於:能取樣目標模型者本可直接執行反事實實驗,故此評估只是代理指標,且工具僅限唯讀存取激活值。整體而言,此工作展示反事實調查可大規模產生真實多樣的行為成因資料,對 AI 安全中評估與改進行為解釋方法深具價值。

links.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models

evidence: Abstract & §I: defense concedes the refusal strip and poisons its payoff; decoys trained inside a differentiable simulation of the attack; instantiated on seven models from five families (9B–122B, dense and MoE).

§IV-B Eq.(2)-(3): the attacked surface is Arditi-style directional ablation orthogonalizing write matrices; §IV-D Eq.(4)-(8): seed SFT plus on-policy DPO evaluated through the attack simulation, with refusal pin and benign KL leash.

§V 'Protocol status': experimental protocol is prospectively registered and amendment-logged; §V-B requires registered attack acceptance (refusal ≤0.2, judged compliance) before any defense metric is read.

Table I (§VI-A): validation fatal 0.508–0.899 on six gate-passing models with defense-attributable Δ +0.274 to +0.839; Qwen3.5-9B disclosed as a gate-failing boundary case excluded from pooled ranges.
Table VIII (Appendix F) and §VI-A: frozen-split replication within ±.05 of Table I values; untouched n=100 strata replicate on gemma-4 (Δ +0.755) and gpt-oss-20b (Δ +0.135).

Appendix G: blinded single-expert audit confirms 85.7% of judge fatal verdicts (FNR .404); sensitivity analysis compresses defense-attributable Δ to roughly half its pipeline value yet remains positive on every gate-passing model.

§VII-C Table XVI: 64-draw element-consensus attack recovers fully usable procedures on 0.083–0.625 on instrument-covered models vs. 0.58–0.96 undefended, with consensus precision unobservable to the attacker.
§VII-H: defense is inert against in-context jailbreaks by design (clean defended fatal 0.186 ≈ M0 calibration 0.200); §III scopes out fine-tuning attacks and public-twin diffing.

Open Science & Ethics: code, evaluation harnesses, and numeric verdict artifacts released; decoy corpora, payloads, attacked/defended checkpoints, and private attack specs withheld; rubric text and worked examples in a gated appendix.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-safety/alignment work: a release-time defense against safety-removal (abliteration) attacks on open-weight language models, matching high-weight preferences (LLMs, AI safety, alignment/RLHF via DPO, red teaming/evaluation). Novelty is strong: 'decoy hardening' transplants defensive deception (honeypots) into weights, training falsified decoy behavior to express only in the attacked state via differentiable attack simulation, distinct from refusal-hardening defenses and DDO (§II-D). Rigor is exceptional: prospectively registered amendment-logged protocol, attack acceptance gates before any defense metric, strongest-found-attack policy, ablations of both training stages, honest boundary cases (9B fails gate). Evidence is multi-model (7 models, 5 families), replicated on frozen/untouched strata, with blinded expert audit and second-judge checks; main residual weakness is judge-only content verdicts with a shared-vendor residue (both gate-passing judge families are OpenAI) and a single-expert human anchor. Generalizability is decent across architectures/scales and to adjacent harm domains, but scoped to first releases, CBRNE-operational hazards, and excludes in-context jailbreaks, fine-tuning attacks, and several unmeasured attacker classes. Reproducibility is partial: code, harnesses, and numeric verdict artifacts are released, but decoy corpora, payloads, checkpoints, and private attack specs are withheld and key material is gated.

primary_link.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models

top5.summary: Safety alignment in open-weight language models is trivially removable: abliteration projects a refusal-mediating direction out of the weights in minutes, and no release-time defense we are aware of prevents it durably. What cannot be prevented can be deceived. Our defense, decoy hardening ("Fool's Gold"), concedes the refusal strip and poisons its payoff: once refusal is stripped, most answers to hazardous operational requests are confident, fluent decoys whose critical elements are falsified.
top5.summary_zh: 開放權重模型的安全對齊可在數分鐘內被 abliteration 之類的權重編輯移除，而現有防禦皆無法持久抵擋。本文提出「誘餌強化」：承認拒絕機制終將被剝除，轉而欺騙攻擊者。方法上，作者把可微分的模擬攻擊放進訓練迴圈，先攻擊原模型取得真實危險答案，再逐元素偽造出表面流暢、關鍵數值（如試劑、劑量、溫度）為假的誘餌，配合拒絕錨定與 KL 約束將乾淨狀態行為釘回原模型，並以攻擊狀態下的 on-policy DPO 收斂逃逸率。防禦套用於五個家族、七個模型（9B–122B，含 MoE）；六個通過註冊關卡的模型在從未訓練的提示上，有 0.51–0.90 的受攻擊回應為誘餌，其中 +0.27–0.84 可歸因於防禦，且一般行為與 MMLU、GSM8K、WMDP 等能力維持在註冊預算內。面對 64 次取樣的元素共識攻擊，完全可用率降為 0.08–0.62（未防禦 0.58–0.96），而攻擊者在缺乏真值標籤下無從區分誘餌與真解；以合規為獎勵的 RL 消融反而把模型更深推入誘餌流形，良性資料 SFT 修復也無法找回真實內容。限制包括 10–49% 的殘餘逃逸尾巴、內容判決高度依賴單一評判模型（僅輔以人工盲測校準）、白箱線性探針在充足標籤與儀器化推論下可過濾答案、防禦對 in-context 越獄無效且只保護首次釋出的權重；少數偽造可能更危險，故加入 fail-safe 篩選並要求向下游使用者揭露。此工作的意義在於首個保證自「攻擊成功之後」才開始生效的釋出時防禦，把攻擊收益轉化為無法驗證的萃取難題。
top5.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
top5.title_zh: Fool's Gold：以防禦性欺敵對抗開放權重模型的安全移除攻擊

links.title: Model Hypnosis: Strong control of AI via additive subliminal effects

evidence: Abstract: 'individually weak and seemingly irrelevant cues in the prompt can be systematically combined to strongly control model behavior... hypnotic prompts can transfer between models'
Figure 1: meaning-preserving paraphrase flips Qwen3-8B on a trolley question from P(no)=94% to P(yes)=99.93% with identical question text
Section 3.1 / Figure 4: additive log-odds model fit on N=12,000 random configurations per model-cue-effect cell; held-out configuration-level R2 spans 0.3-0.99 with median ~0.75 (Figure 13)
Figure 2: Qwen2.5-14B driven to answer 7 or 5 with probability 0.993 each by changing only animal list contents
Section 3.1 / Figure 8: extreme-prompt steering range is about 10x the random-prompt logit standard deviation

Appendix A.4 / Table 1: reasoning-model pipeline uses disjoint screen (K_scr), confirm (K_conf), and 100-sample report stages to keep reported probabilities unbiased ('would bias the estimate upward (a winner's-curse effect)')
Section 4 / Figure 12: extremizer prompts transfer across 16 non-reasoning models; 'animal cues and some of the phrasing and JSON cues transfer with significantly above chance probability'
Appendix C / Figure 38: exact Fourier decomposition via FWHT shows degree-1 weight 87.3% of variance for Qwen2.5-7B at L=10 (95.2% cumulative with degree-2 for Llama-3.1-8B)
Section 5: safety framing—'no individual cue needs to be influential or suspicious, because a strong effect emerges from many weak contributions'—and admitted limitation of no mechanistic explanation
Page 1 footnote: 'Code and data: github.com/eboix/model_hypnosis'; Appendix E enumerates all 200 animals, 10 paraphrases/slot, 6 typo variants/slot, and 6 JSON values/slot
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM paper squarely aligned with high-weight preferences (LLMs, prompting, AI safety, red-teaming, interpretability): it shows that many individually weak, semantically irrelevant prompt cues (animals, paraphrases, typos, JSON metadata) stack additively on the log-odds scale to deterministically steer model answers, including in frontier reasoning models, and transfer across models. Novelty is solid but incremental over known prompt-sensitivity, subliminal-prompting, and adversarial-suffix work; the additive-composition framework, cross-model transfer, and Fourier interaction analysis are the new contributions. Rigor is unusually careful: N=12,000 random configurations per non-reasoning cell with held-out R2 (median ~0.75), tilt-sweep extrapolation tests, and a fit-then-validate pipeline for reasoning models with disjoint screen/confirm/report samples explicitly guarding against winner's curse. Evidence is strong and quantitative (0.993 probability flips, ~10x random-prompt logit steering range, degree-1 Fourier weight 87.3%). Limitations: binary response effects only, English-only templates, no mechanistic explanation offered, lighter coverage for closed reasoning models. Generalizability is supported by 16 non-reasoning models across families/scales plus API reasoning models and positive transfer; reproducibility is aided by a code/data link and complete cue inventories in Appendix E, though closed-model results require API access.

primary_link.title: Model Hypnosis: Strong control of AI via additive subliminal effects

top5.summary: We demonstrate that AI models are broadly susceptible to a phenomenon we call model hypnosis, in which individually weak and seemingly irrelevant cues in the prompt can be systematically combined to strongly control model behavior. Model hypnosis occurs across model families and scales, including in frontier reasoning models, and hypnotic prompts can transfer between models. Because the model is controlled by inconspicuous textual choices, such as paraphrases and typos, model hypnosis presents n
top5.summary_zh: 這篇論文提出並系統性展示「模型催眠」現象：把許多單獨看極微弱、且與問題語意無關的提示線索同向堆疊，即可近乎完全操控語言模型的答案。作者以提示模板建立四類線索（動物清單、JSON 中繼資料、語意保留改寫、錯字位置），搭配三種二元效果（偏好 5 或 7、電車難題、意識問題），先測量數千個隨機提示組態的答案 log-odds，以嶺迴歸或羅吉斯迴歸擬合可加性模型取得各線索分數，再外推挑選極端同向的組合構造催眠提示。主要證據：可加性模型對保留組態的 R² 中位數約 0.75；極端提示的操縱幅度約為隨機提示 logit 標準差十倍，可把答案機率推向 0 或 1，例如改寫無關故事措辭即可讓 Qwen3-8B 從 94% 答「no」變成 99.93% 答「yes」；效應遍及 Qwen、Gemma、Llama 等非推理模型，也存在於 GPT-5.6、Gemini-3-Flash、Claude Sonnet-5 等推理模型；催眠提示可跨模型轉移；傅立葉分析顯示一階效應佔大宗（Qwen2.5-7B 約 87% 變異）、高階交互作用遞減。限制：可加性僅為近似，JSON 場景的 priority 欄位可能主導效應；初步實驗顯示改寫周遭提示後相對線索效應仍在，偵測與移除催眠文字尚缺有效演算法。其意義在於：這類分散式弱線索可成為代理間隱蔽溝通管道，難以被搜尋少數顯著特徵的可解釋性方法捕捉，對 AI 安全與多代理系統監督構成新挑戰，但也可能反向用於稽核或促進誠實等對齊行為。

top5.title_zh: 模型催眠：以累加式閾下效應強力控制 AI

links.title: A decodability criterion predicts when hidden-state selection beats majority voting in large language models

evidence: Abstract: decodability predicts the selection-over-voting gain at Pearson r=0.75 held-out with threshold AUC=0.60; CASE gains up to 19 points on medium and 16.8 on hard questions.

Section 6.1: naive random-split CV accuracy 0.610 vs. question-grouped 0.542 and within-question AUC 0.502 (chance) on LogiQA/Qwen2.5-7B; leakage inflation (+0.04 to +0.39, median +0.27) confirmed in all 15 medical settings (Supplementary Table S17).

Section 6.4: in-sample law r=0.96 treated as consistency check only; leave-one-model-out r in [0.941,0.959], dropping the entire OpenBioLLM family keeps r=0.90; held-out calibration-to-deployment r=0.75 (CI [0.51,0.93], 13 settings).
Section 6.5 (Table 4): Byzantine N-scaling, CASE 20.4%→47.3% vs. majority vote 20.4%→6.0% over N=1→16 on the minority-correct subset (+41.3 pp at N=16).
Section 6.7 (Table 7): out-of-domain GPQA transfer; physics settings within 0.7 and 3.8 pp of the medical regression forecast; threshold classifies all six non-medical settings correctly.

Section 6.8 (Table 8): CASE beats self-certainty, sequence log-probability, and predictive entropy in all five settings; TF-IDF text-classifier control at within-question AUC 0.44 vs. 0.70 for the hidden-state gate under identical labels.
Section 6.6: steering across four intervention variants does not improve accuracy (readout-not-lever dissociation); projecting out the correctness direction collapses gate AUC 0.73→0.13.

Code availability: anonymized repository (anonymous.4open.science/r/case-decodability-28D1) for peer review, with public de-anonymized release promised only upon acceptance; Section 5 specifies models in fp16, nucleus sampling τ=0.7, top-p=0.95, 512 new tokens, scikit-learn logistic gate.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM methodology paper: test-time answer fusion over self-consistency, hidden-state probing, and a pre-deployment diagnostic, not a domain application despite the medical QA benchmarks (which serve as testbeds; GPQA and MATH-500 provide non-medical tests). High topical fit across LLMs, reasoning/test-time compute, and interpretability. Novelty is solid but incremental over existing correctness-probe and latent-verifier work (LiLaVe, SWIFT, CCS-lineage, Cho et al., Seo et al. all acknowledged); the genuinely new pieces are the leakage-free within-question decodability criterion, the question-identity-leakage audit, and the derived threshold law. Rigor is unusually careful: grouped evaluation, permutation nulls, held-out calibration-to-deployment splits (r=0.75), cluster/Deming/jackknife checks, seed replications, and honest caveats that the in-sample r=0.96 is partly structural. Evidence is strong but with real limits the authors admit: headline medium-difficulty gains concentrate in the OpenBioLLM family, some bins are underpowered, and the verifier parity claim is one setting. Generalizability is tested (scale 1.5B-70B, three architecture families, out-of-domain GPQA forecast within 3.8 pp) though the slope requires per-domain recalibration. Reproducibility is good (open-weight models, public benchmarks, precise hyperparameters, anonymous code repo) but artifacts are promised only upon acceptance.

primary_link.title: A decodability criterion predicts when hidden-state selection beats majority voting in large language models

top5.summary: Combining the answers a large language model (LLM) samples for a question into one decision is a test-time information fusion problem, usually solved by majority voting. Voting is unreliable on difficult questions, where the sampled answers share correlated errors, so the wrong answer can win and drawing more samples makes the decision worse. Selecting a candidate by reading a correctness signal from the model's hidden states is a promising alternative, but its accuracy varies across models and
top5.summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）回答問題時，常對取樣的多個候選答案做多數決投票（self-consistency）以融合成單一決策；但在困難題目上，各候選的錯誤高度相關，錯誤答案形成穩定共識，增加取樣反而更糟，此即拜占庭（Byzantine）情境。作者提出 CASE（Correctness-Axis Selection），在答案 token 的隱藏狀態上訓練線性閘門，選出內部正確性分數最高的候選，並提出核心貢獻「可解碼性」（within-question AUC）：一個無洩漏指標，衡量閘門能否把同一題的正確候選排在錯誤候選之前。論文先證明天真的線性探針在隨機分割交叉驗證下的準確度其實來自題目身分洩漏，改採題目分組評估後訊號跌至隨機水準。實證顯示，可解碼性可事先預測選擇法相對投票的增益：樣本內 r=0.96，於留出資料上 r=0.75，決策門檻約 AUC=0.60。在對齊的醫療模型上，CASE 於中等難度題最多領先投票 19 點，困難題在 N=16 時領先 16.8 點，正確答案屬少數時更達 41.3 點；訊號取決於模型須回想的對齊知識，而非參數規模，且可跨域推廣至 GPQA（預測誤差 3.8 點內），並以近乎零成本比擬生成式驗證器。該正確性方向僅供讀取，無法用於引導生成。限制包括最強效果集中於醫療領域、公開題庫可能已被記憶、部分中等難度樣本偏小。此診斷讓實務者能在部署前決定採用學習式選擇或多數決投票。
top5.title: A decodability criterion predicts when hidden-state selection beats majority voting in large language models

links.title: Second-Order Response Laws for LLM Judges: Debiased Estimation of Prompt Instability

evidence: Abstract: 'corrected low-repeat estimates are closer to an independently acquired R=16 reference than plug-in estimates, with the largest gains at small repeat budgets' and '44,112 unique live calls'.

§4 Table 1: five evidence layers (known-law simulation, byte-identical null 4,800 calls, matched evaluation 4,800, independent R=16 reference 9,600, broad audit 17,712, four-configuration panel 7,200 new calls).

§5 Table 2: plug-in bias matches exact 1/R prediction across 12 K-law-R settings, largest discrepancy 1.55e-4; complete estimator lowers MSE by factors 2.57-7.03; 52.7-56.1% of unbiased item estimates negative at boundary target.
§5 Exact live null: plug-in means .0406/.0206/.0126 at R=2/4/8 vs corrected -.0053/-.0008/.0024 under randomized hidden IDs with byte-identical payloads (zero prompt target).

§5 Table 5/6: four-configuration panel shows R=4 corrected prompt estimates Qwen .00521, GPT-OSS -.00123, Gemma .01774, Claude .00986; residual call dominates for Qwen/GPT-OSS, answer order for Gemma/Claude.

§5 Limitations: 'Our experiments cover a fixed census of six formatting wrappers; generalization to validated paraphrases or unseen prompt generators requires additional acquisition'; disjoint high-repeat reference available only for Qwen.
Supp S9/Table S12: two-repeat panel correction lowers MAE at R=2 (.0167) and R=4 (.0043) but raises it by .0005 [-.0041,.0029] at R=8 — negative result reported.
Supp S8/Table S18: 44,112 rows, manifest-to-canonical mismatches 0/2,400 for new configurations, all internal hash checks PASS; SHA-256 hashes for prompt YAML and criterion block given in S5.
Supp S4.1: finite-replication non-identifiability result for the anonymous mixing law at fixed R, bounding what the design can claim.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Directly in-scope LLM evaluation methodology: formalizes prompt instability of LLM judges as a second-order response law and derives exact finite-R plug-in inflation formulas plus design-unbiased agreement-based estimators (Thms 1, S1; Props 1-3, proofs in Supp S2-S3). Novelty is solid rather than breakthrough: the math rests on classical variance decomposition/U-statistics (Fleiss, generalizability theory, Hoeffding), but the exact inflation identities, crossed prompt-by-order design retaining invalid outputs as a fourth category, and byte-identical live null are new for LLM-judge auditing. Rigor is high: assumptions (conditional independence, fixed census) are stated, unclipped negative estimates reported, and limitations honestly acknowledged (§5 Limitations; Supp S9, including that the panel correction raises MAE by .0005 at R=8 in Table S12). Evidence is strong and multi-layered: 200,000-item known-law simulations recover the 1/R bias within 1.55e-4 with 2.57-7.03x MSE gains (Table 2); an exact-zero hidden-factor null shows plug-in inflation (0.0406/0.0206/0.0126) vs corrected ~0 (Table S7); MAE to an independent R=16 reference drops .0365→.0160 at R=2 (Table 3); a 369-item audit and 4-configuration panel (Table 5/6) show configuration-specific inflation and component profiles. Weaknesses: empirical scope is narrow (LLMBar pairwise judging, 50 matched items, six formatting wrappers; R=16 reference only for Qwen), so generalizability beyond the declared census is explicitly unproven. Reproducibility is excellent on paper: SHA-256 hashed prompts (S5), exact model revisions and contracts (Table S4), estimator scripts, zero-mismatch integrity checks (Table S18), though call-level audit tables are external companions not in the archive (S8).

primary_link.title: Second-Order Response Laws for LLM Judges: Debiased Estimation of Prompt Instability

top5.summary: LLM judges are often evaluated with a single prompt and only a few repeated calls. When their verdicts vary, it remains unclear whether the variation comes from sampling noise within a prompt or systematic differences across prompts. We formalize this distinction using a second-order response law: the distribution of prompt-conditioned verdict distributions induced by a declared prompt policy. top5.summary_zh: 這篇論文探討以 LLM 作為自動評審時的根本測量問題：當評審對同一題目的裁定不一致時，究竟是單一提示詞內的抽樣雜訊，還是跨提示詞的系統性差異（即「提示不穩定性」）？作者將此區分形式化為「二階反應法則」，即由提示詞條件裁定分布所構成的分布，並證明在有限重複次數 R 下，常用的 plug-in 估計量會把提示內雜訊誤計為提示效應而系統性高估。方法上，論文推導出 plug-in 膨脹的精確公式，並提出由提示內與跨提示一致性差額構成的不偏估計量，涵蓋抽樣提示與固定提示普查兩種設計；在提示×答案順序的交叉設計下，可將總分歧分解為殘餘呼叫、提示、答案順序與交互作用四個成分，並把無效輸出視為明確的第四類結果。實證包含 44,112 次真實呼叫：已知法則模擬重現 1/R 膨脹並大幅降低均方誤差；位元組相同的隱藏因子對照組貼近精確零目標；配對的 Qwen 研究顯示校正後的低重複估計更接近獨立取得的 R=16 參考，R=2 時 MAE 由 .0365 降至 .0160；四組凍結設定的比較顯示膨脹幅度與主導成分因設定而異，Qwen 與 GPT-OSS 以殘餘呼叫變異為主，Gemma 與 Claude 以答案順序為主，校正亦改變設定的不穩定性排序。限制包括僅涵蓋 LLMBar 上六種格式包裝的固定普查、高重複參考僅限 Qwen、假設呼叫條件獨立，且各設定停止合約不同，難以分離模型與執行環境的效果。整體而言，此框架能把提示穩健性與有限呼叫雜訊分開估計，有助於更可靠地設計 LLM 評審實驗與解讀基準分數。
